title: Attention Is All You Need
authors: Vaswani, Shazeer, Parmar, Uszkoreit, Jones, Gomez, Kaiser, Polosukhin
content: The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks that include an encoder and a decoder. The best performing models also connect the encoder and decoder through an attention mechanism. We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely. Experiments on two machine translation tasks show these models to be superior in quality while being more parallelizable and requiring significantly less time to train. Our model achieves 28.4 BLEU on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task, improving over the existing best results, including ensembles, by over 2 BLEU. On the WMT 2014 English-to-French translation task, our model establishes a new single-model state-of-the-art BLEU score of 41.8 after training for 3.5 days on eight GPUs.

title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
content: We introduce a new language representation model called BERT, which stands for Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers. Unlike recent language representation models, BERT is designed to pre-train deep bidirectional representations from unlabeled text by jointly conditioning on both left and right context in all layers. As a result, the pre-trained BERT model can be fine-tuned with just one additional output layer to create state-of-the-art models for a wide range of tasks, such as question answering and language inference. BERT conceptually simple and widely applicable. It obtains state-of-the-art results on eleven natural language processing tasks.

title: GPT-4 Technical Report
content: We report the development of GPT-4, a large-scale, multimodal model which can accept image and text inputs and produce text outputs. GPT-4 exhibits more complex reasoning capabilities than previous models. We demonstrate that GPT-4 outperforms previous state-of-the-art models on a wide range of benchmarks, including academic and professional exams in multiple domains, achieving at or near the human upper band. GPT-4 can also perform creative writing, answer questions about images, and write code in a variety of programming languages.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
authors: Lewis, Perez, Piktus, Petroni, Karpukhin, Goyal, Küttler, Balewicki, Ranzato, Goldstein
content: Large pre-trained language models have been shown to store factual knowledge in their parameters, and achieve state-of-the-art results when fine-tuned on downstream NLP tasks. However, their ability to access and precisely manipulate knowledge is still limited, and hence on knowledge-intensive tasks, their生成 quality lags. An appealing alternative is to make use of non-parametric memory, such as a dense vector index of document encodings, accessible with a differentiable neural retrieval model. In this work, we propose a general-purpose finetunable hybrid model, which combines a parametric memory (a pre-trained seq2seq model) with a non-parametric memory (a dense vector index of Wikipedia), accessed with a neural reader.

title: Vector Database Search: A Survey on Approaches and Challenges
content: Vector databases have become critical infrastructure for similarity search in applications including recommendation systems, image retrieval, and semantic text search. This survey provides a comprehensive overview of vector database search algorithms, including approximate nearest neighbor methods (HNSW, IVF, LSH), distance metrics (cosine similarity, Euclidean, inner product), and hybrid indexing strategies that combine full-text search with vector similarity. We discuss the challenges of scaling to billions of vectors, maintaining index freshness under high insertion rates, and optimizing query latency while preserving recall.

title: Hybrid Search: Combining Sparse and Dense Retrieval for Passage Ranking
content: Modern information retrieval systems increasingly combine sparse retrieval methods such as BM25 with dense retrieval approaches using pre-trained language model embeddings. This hybrid approach leverages the complementary strengths of both paradigms: sparse methods excel at exact keyword matching while dense methods capture semantic similarity. In this paper, we propose a unified scoring framework that learns optimal weights for combining full-text relevance scores with cosine similarity distances. Our experiments on MS MARCO and TREC benchmarks demonstrate that hybrid search consistently outperforms either method alone, with improvements up to 12% in MRR@10.

title: Seekdb: A High-Performance Vector Database with MySQL Compatibility
content: We present seekdb, a vector database that provides native support for high-dimensional vector indexing and full-text search within a MySQL-compatible interface. seekdb introduces a unified query execution engine that can simultaneously evaluate MATCH...AGAINST full-text predicates and COSINE_DISTANCE vector predicates in a single SQL statement, with adaptive cost-based optimization for hybrid retrieval. The system supports HNSW and IVF vector index types, multiple distance metrics, and full-text search with IK tokenizer for Chinese language documents. Benchmark results show seekdb achieving 95% recall at 1000 QPS on 100-million vector workloads.

title: Efficient Similarity Search in High-Dimensional Spaces
content: We propose a new navigable small-world graph algorithm called HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) for approximate nearest neighbor search. We build a data structure based on multi-layered proximity graph where the upper layers contain the most distant links, creating a navigable small world structure. The search is performed by a greedy algorithm starting from the top layer. We show experimentally that our approach provides logarithmic complexity of the search procedure and outperforms previous state-of-the-art methods in terms of recall-latency tradeoff for high-dimensional vectors with up to thousands of dimensions.

title: Chinese Text Segmentation and Full-Text Indexing for Information Retrieval
content: Chinese information retrieval requires effective text segmentation because Chinese text lacks explicit word boundaries. We propose an enhanced approach for Chinese full-text indexing that integrates the IK tokenizer with custom domain dictionaries for scientific paper titles and abstracts. Our system supports MATCH AGAINST queries with both natural language mode and boolean mode for Chinese text. Experimental evaluation on a corpus of 2 million Chinese academic papers shows that our method achieves 92% tokenization accuracy and reduces query latency by 40% compared to character-level n-gram approaches.

title: Embedding Models for Semantic Search: A Practical Comparison
content: Dense retrieval relies on embedding models to convert text into fixed-length vectors suitable for approximate nearest neighbor search. This work provides a practical comparison of embedding models for semantic search tasks, including sentence transformers (all-MiniLM-L6-v2, all-mpnet-base-v2), the BGE series, and commercial API-based models. We evaluate these models across multiple dimensions: retrieval quality (MRR, NDCG), inference speed, vector dimension tradeoffs, and domain-specific performance on scientific papers. Our benchmarks show that model selection can impact retrieval quality by up to 15% for scientific document search, with larger dimension vectors (768 vs 384) providing marginal improvements.
